sections.label: AV trial regulatory framework
sections.summary: LTA requires AVs to pass a safety assessment and developers to have accident mitigation plans including a trained safety driver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The LTA has put in place a robust regulatory framework for AV trials to minimise the possibility of accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: First, AVs must demonstrate basic roadworthiness and capabilities by passing a safety assessment, before they can even be trialled on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Second, AVs developers must have robust accident mitigation plans for the trials, including having a safety driver who is trained to swiftly take control of the AV, whenever necessary.

sections.label: AV liability and data logging
sections.summary: AV liability will likely be resolved through proof of fault and common law, and test AVs must log travel data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As with accidents involving human-driven vehicles, it is likely that issues of liability for AVs will be resolved through proof of fault and existing common law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We will require all test AVs to log travel data to facilitate accident investigations and liability claims.

sections.label: Penalty for obstructing AVs
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng asked about the rationale for the $5,000 maximum penalty for first-time offenders who obstruct AVs during trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the rationale for the maximum penalty of $5,000 for first-time offenders who obstruct AVs during trials.

sections.label: Private hire car vocational licence
sections.summary: Private hire car drivers must obtain a vocational licence with the taxi demerit point system and similar Conduct Rules, with no licensing fees for booking operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We take issues related to the safety of commuters very seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This is why we will be requiring private hire car drivers to obtain a vocational licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: And when we do so, this vocational licence framework will impose on private hire car drivers the same demerit point system that is currently applied across the taxi drivers today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Private hire car drivers will also have to abide, under this framework, to similar Conduct Rules as taxi drivers − cleanliness, dressing and all those.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As we are not planning to license private hire car booking service operators for now, there will be no licencing fees.

sections.label: Child seat rule for PHCs
sections.summary: The decision is to err on the side of ensuring the safety of child passengers on private hire cars rather than exempting them from the child seat rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Having said this, I do take your point that an argument can, indeed, be made to similarly exempt private hire cars from the child seat rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But for now, we have decided to err on the side of ensuring the safety of child passengers on PHCs.

sections.label: LTA power over taxi licences
sections.summary: LTA has the power today to revoke or suspend the licences of taxi operators which do not comply with licensing conditions or directives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: To put this in context, as I think Mr Ang also mentioned just now, LTA has the power today to revoke or suspend the licences of taxi operators which do not comply with LTA's licensing conditions or directives.

sections.label: PHC licence for non-citizens
sections.summary: Non-Singapore citizens get a PHC Drivers' Vocational Licence only if employed by chauffeured services companies, and two years' driving experience is deemed adequate for passenger safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Non-Singapore citizens will be granted a PHC Drivers' Vocational Licence only if they are employees of chauffeured services companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: And as for a minimum age criterion, our view is that requiring PHC drivers to have a minimum driving experience of two years should be adequate to reasonably ensure passenger safety.

sections.label: Carpooling services not regulated
sections.summary: Unlike PHC services, where drivers provide rides as income, carpooling services are not intended to be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This is different from PHC services, where the intent is for the drivers to provide rides as a source of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Hence, we do not intend to regulate carpooling services.

sections.label: PAB maximum device speed
sections.summary: New technical requirements introduced last year limit PABs to a maximum device speed of 25 km/h.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The new technical requirements for PABs, introduced last year, limit PABs to a maximum device speed of 25 km/h, which is roughly my cycling speed.

sections.label: Automation levels under laws
sections.summary: Under the laws, levels 3, 4 and 5 cover high automation to full automation, which is driverless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Under our laws, it will be under levels 3, 4 and 5 from high automation to full automation which is driverless.

sections.label: Non-compliant devices liable to seizure
sections.summary: For non-compliant PAB and PMD devices, once non-compliant, the device is liable to be seized.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For such non-compliant PAB and PMD devices, once you are non-compliant, you are liable to be seized.

sections.label: Offences are seizable offences
sections.summary: The key point is that all these offences are seizable offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The key point is all these offences are seizable offences.

sections.label: Taxi operator licensing fees doubled
sections.summary: LTA recently doubled taxi operators' licensing fees from 0.01% to 0.02%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Recently, LTA doubled the licensing fees for taxi operators from 0.01% to 0.02%.

sections.label: Drivers joining other PHC operators
sections.summary: A driver affiliated with a suspended PHC operator can join another operator to provide PHC services during the suspension.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When issued with the suspension order on a PHC booking service operator, for example Operator A, can the affiliated driver of Operator A join Operator B to provide PHC services during the suspension period?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: And whether a driver can drive for another service operator, the answer is also yes.

sections.label: Balanced light-touch regulatory stance
sections.summary: A balanced, light-touch regulatory stance protects passenger and road user safety while letting these technologies flourish.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We must have due regard for the safety of passengers and other road users.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, adopting a balanced, light-touch regulatory stance that protects the safety of passengers and other road users, and yet ensures that these technologies can flourish.

sections.label: AV deployment and driver reskilling
sections.summary: Widespread AV deployment is some 10 to 15 years away, and the Government will progressively help Singaporeans who drive for a living acquire new skills.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Widespread deployment of AV technology is still some 10, maybe 15 years away and, progressively, the Government will put in place programmes to help Singaporeans who drive for a living to acquire new skills and take on higher value-added jobs in an AV world.

sections.label: Clause 6 conditional high automation
sections.summary: Clause 6, read with clause 3(a) amendments, applies to motor vehicles with conditional high and full automation under SAE levels 3, 4 and 5.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Clause 6, read with the amendments in clause 3(a), applies to motor vehicles with conditional high and full automation, as defined in levels 3, 4 and 5 of the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) International J3016.

sections.label: Five-year regulatory sandbox period
sections.summary: The regulatory sandbox is limited to five years, after which the Ministry will consider permanent legislation or seek further extension.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As this is an emerging technology, the provisions will provide the flexibility needed to assess the appropriate regulatory response more quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have limited this regulatory sandbox to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: At the end of five years, the Ministry will consider enacting more permanent legislation or return to Parliament to further extend the period of the sandbox.

sections.label: PHC driver licensing and decals
sections.summary: The amendments require all PHC drivers providing chauffeured services to obtain vocational licences, and chauffeur-driven PHCs must display LTA-issued tamper-evident decals by mid-year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Last year, I had said that we will take a more balanced and sensible approach in regulating this industry, with the safety of commuters as our priority.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hence, by the amendments, all PHC drivers providing chauffeured services will be required to obtain vocational licences.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For identification purposes, all chauffeur-driven PHCs must be affixed with tamper-evident decals issued by LTA, by the middle of the year.

sections.label: Registrar's general suspension order
sections.summary: Clause 34 introduces section 110A empowering the Registrar of Vehicles to issue a general suspension order barring all PHC drivers affiliated with a particular PHC booking service operator from driving for that operator.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Clause 34 introduces a new section 110A which empowers the Registrar of Vehicles to issue a general suspension order that bars all PHC drivers affiliated with a particular PHC booking service operator from driving for that operator.

sections.label: Composition sums and dangerous driving penalties
sections.summary: Clause 38 raises the maximum composition sum to 50% of the maximum fine or $5,000, whichever is lower, and clause 20 raises reckless or dangerous driving penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This low cap restricts the ability of LTA and the Traffic Police to calibrate the composition sums offered according to the severity of offences and to deter repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hence, clause 38 increases the maximum composition sum for all offences in the Road Traffic Act to 50% of the maximum fine prescribed for the offence, or $5,000, whichever is lower.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Clause 20 raises the penalties for the offence of "reckless or dangerous driving" from $3,000 to $5,000 for the first offence, and $5,000 to $10,000 for the second or subsequent offence.

sections.label: Fast-changing transportation landscape
sections.summary: A key reason the amendments are needed is the fast-changing landscape of transportation in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A key reason why these amendments are needed is because of the fast-changing landscape of transportation in Singapore.

sections.label: Bill's AV and PMD amendments
sections.summary: The Bill's aim covers amendments relating to the trial and use of AVs and those relating to power-assisted bicycles and PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The aim of this Bill is to do exactly that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: They are: (a) the amendments relating to the trial and use of AVs; and (b) those that relate to power-assisted bicycles and PMDs.

sections.label: AV trials and road user safety
sections.summary: As companies such as nuTonomy begin trials on roads, precautions must ensure the safety and well-being of all other road users are protected, with the Government adopting a balanced, light-touch regulatory stance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, as we allow companies, such as nuTonomy, to begin conducting trials on our roads, it is imperative that we take all precautions to ensure that the safety and well-being of all other road users are adequately provided for and protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I do, however, fully agree and appreciate Second Minister for Transport Mr Ng Chee Meng's position in his Second Reading of the Bill that the Government will be adopting "a balanced, light-touch, regulatory stance that protects the safety of Singaporeans and yet ensures that these technologies can flourish." It is important that Singapore remain in the forefront of cutting-edge technology and not shy away from taking the lead.

sections.label: Support for PMD amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill's amendments to regulate power-assisted bicycles and PMDs, having earlier raised concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I had raised several concerns I had about power-assisted bicycles and PMDs and I shall not repeat them here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am in full support of the amendments proposed in this Bill to regulate power-assisted bicycles and PMDs.

sections.label: No training for PAB riders
sections.summary: Riders of power-assisted bicycles, unlike motorcycles, are not required to receive formal training before operating on roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Unlike motorcycles, riders of power-assisted bicycles are not required to receive any formal training prior to operating the bicycles on our roads.

sections.label: Training for power-assisted bicycle riders
sections.summary: The speaker says PABs carry motorcycle-like risk and asks why riders are not trained in road traffic rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: While I agree that power-assisted bicycles are not as powerful in engine capacity as motorcycles, they are, in all reality, low-powered motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: When allowed to operate on roads, they carry the same risk profile as other motorcycle riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If these power-assisted bicycle riders do not have formal training on road traffic rules and other common road traffic etiquette, the risk and likelihood of accident involving power-assisted bicycles on our roads increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I applaud the move taken by the Government to register and license all power-assisted bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But, having done so, why not take the next step in ensuring that all riders of such bicycles be adequately trained, not only in using them, but also on the basic road traffic rules that all other road users, such as drivers and motorcyclists are made to do?

sections.label: Scope of the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a framework for autonomous vehicle trials, regulates affiliated private hire car drivers, and covers forfeiture of non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among other things, the Bill is seeking to establish a regulatory framework for the undertaking of trials and use on Singapore roads for autonomous or driverless vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill is also seeking to regulate holders of vocational licences who are affiliated drivers of private hire car booking service operators providing ride-sourcing services like Uber.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also deals with forfeiture of seized non-compliant power-assisted bicycles and personal mobility devices.

sections.label: Self-driving car and lorry collision
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported on 19 October last year a collision between a self-driving car and a lorry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On 19 October last year, it was reported in The Straits Times that a self-driving car and a lorry collided, in what is believed to be the first accident in Singapore involving an AV.

sections.label: Liability for driverless car accidents
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether driverless car owners will remain defendants in all accidents caused by manufacturing defects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the issue of liability, will owners of driverless cars continue to be defendants in all accidents when it is clear that an accident has been caused by some manufacturing defects?

sections.label: Clause 34 ride-sourcing penalty
sections.summary: MP questions clause 34's general suspension order barring all drivers of a ride-sourcing company after one driver's conviction, unlike the 2015 Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the proposed amendments involving private hire cars providing ride-sourcing services like Uber, I am particularly curious about the proposed penalty under clause 34 of the Bill which provides for a general suspension order that can bar every driver of a ride-sourcing company like Uber for a period of time as a result of another driver in the same company being convicted for an offence under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The proposed penalty is not only unnecessarily harsh, it is also a penalty that only applies to ride-sourcing companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, the corresponding provision in the Third Party Taxi Booking Service Providers Act 2015 – and this is in section 20 – is not exactly on par with the proposed clause 34 in this Bill in that, under the 2015 Act, it seems that only the taxi booking service providers will be penalised but not all individual drivers under the same service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am concerned that clause 34 may go beyond penalising the ride-sourcing companies to unfairly penalise and prejudice other drivers working for the same companies when compared to taxi drivers under the 2015 Act and, in the process, affecting the livelihood of these drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Why is the Government allowing this particular penalty and the different treatment for drivers of ride-sourcing companies?

sections.label: Amending Road Traffic Act safety
sections.summary: The Government should amend the Road Traffic Act to ensure safety of test drive participants and road users and reduce accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moving forward, similar accidents may continue to occur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, it is essential for the Government to amend the Road Traffic Act to ensure the safety of the people involved in the test drives and the road users, as well as reduce the accident rate.

sections.label: Safer emerging transport services
sections.summary: Amending the Road Traffic Act will enable emerging transport services to be safer and more reliable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amending the Road Traffic Act will enable emerging transport services to be safer and more reliable.

sections.label: Older workers and industry engagement
sections.summary: Speaker hopes agencies communicate with industry players, respect the market and exercise appropriate control, noting Uber Taiwan suspended services after fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many older people may find it difficult to make a career switch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that Government agencies can engage in close communication with the related industry players, especially innovative companies, so as to understand the unique nature of the industry, adopt the right approach, respect the market and exercise appropriate control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recently, Uber in Taiwan has announced suspending their services after being heavily fined by Taiwan's Transport Ministry.

sections.label: Uber outcome and commuters
sections.summary: In this scenario Uber lost, the government did not win, and commuters lost a convenient mode of transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this real-life scenario, Uber lost out, the government also did not win, but most unfortunate of all is that commuters have lost a convenient mode of transport.

sections.label: Smart taxi licence non-renewal
sections.summary: Smart exited the taxi market in 2013 after LTA did not renew its licence for failing quality standards, leaving about 270 drivers unable to ply roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2013, taxi operator Smart had to exit from a lucrative taxi market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Because the company did not have its operator licence renewed by LTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This was due to the fact that the operator had consistently failed to meet quality standards, such as call booking catering rate, accident rate and first inspection passing rate and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Consequently, its fleet of about 270 taxi drivers was unable to ply the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The suspension order of up to a month serves as a deterrent to errant drivers and the PHC booking service providers.

sections.label: Hybrid vehicle road tax
sections.summary: The speaker learned the road tax for a hybrid vehicle was much more than the petrol version, reasoned on a dual-motor basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Almost all went well, until the last minute of the discussion, when I learned that the road tax for the hybrid vehicle which I was about to purchase was much more than the petrol-driven version − being reasoned as having a dual-motor system as a basis of the road tax computation.

sections.label: Driverless AV on public roads
sections.summary: The passage asks whether an AV can be operated on public roads without a driver, meaning driverless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, can an AV be allowed to be operated on our public road without a driver, meaning driverless?

sections.label: Certifying AVs fit for roads
sections.summary: The passage asks how to ensure an AV is certified fit for roads with infrastructure constraints unlike other global cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The third question, how do we ensure that the concerned AV is being certified fit for use on our roads where we have constraints in terms of infrastructure, which is not the same as compared to the other global cities?

sections.label: Operator inside every AV
sections.summary: The passage asks whether every AV must always have an operator inside, even if declared AV-certified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should we not make a point that every AV must always have an operator, that is, a person inside, even though if the vehicle is deemed and declared as AV-certified?

sections.label: New technologies in motor vehicles
sections.summary: Motor vehicles of the same capacity class now have new technologies like turbo, electronic injection and software-controlled powertrain, making similar class vehicles different.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Current motor vehicles with the same capacity class are now packed with an array of new technologies, like turbo and electronic injection engine and more sophisticated software-controlled powertrain, which render "similar" class motor vehicles a completely different machine and performance.

sections.label: Reviewing motor vehicle classification
sections.summary: The passage supports reviewing motor vehicle classification to consider aspects like environmental impact, with LTA managing it through published gazette, and regulations on private hire cabs and drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, this advancement in the automobile industry should motivate us to make a regular self-check on our classification of motor vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe it would be wise if the classification of motor vehicles is to include and consider other aspects, such as impact on our environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I support the need to relook and review our motor vehicle classification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is even heartening to know that in trying to address the need to be quick and nimble in adapting to the fast changes in automotive technologies, the classification of motor vehicles will be managed by LTA through published gazette.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It provides alternatives for those who want to have a chauffeured car and it also provides additional income to many who are willing to work hard.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, for the safety of all commuters and other road users, it is good that we put in place some form of regulations on the operators of private hire cabs and their drivers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The private hire car drivers should go through proper training, adhere to certain rules while carrying passengers and, most of all, be screened to ensure that only those with good character are given a licence.

sections.label: Minimum age of private hire drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the minimum driver age has changed, noting Uber and Grab drivers as young as 21 are currently allowed.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, is there any change in the minimum age of the driver because, currently, for drivers of Uber or Grab cars, those as young as 21 years old are allowed to drive?

sections.label: Nationality of private hire drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister whether any restriction exists on the nationality of private hire car drivers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to ask the Minister: is there any restriction on the nationality of the drivers of these private hire cars?

sections.label: Uber losses and fundraising
sections.summary: The passage states Uber lost about US$1.4 billion in the first six months of 2016 and raised close to US$5 billion that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Uber's losses in the first six months of 2016 was roughly US$1.4 billion and it is projected that its full year loss would hit a record US$3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2016 alone, Uber raised close to US$5 billion in equity and debt to fund its expansion.

sections.label: Rental car and taxi numbers
sections.summary: The passage states rental cars rose from about 19,000 at end-2014 to over 51,000, surpassing taxis, with signs of market saturation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The number of rental cars has increased from about 19,000 at end-2014 to more than 51,000 by the end of last year, far surpassing our taxi population of 27,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Even if we remove the 2% cap on taxi population growth, I am afraid it has become a moot point as, in a Straits Times article on 15 January this year, it was reported that there are signs that the market has hit saturation point with more than 2,000 unhired private hire vehicles and taxis.

sections.label: Support for harsher driving penalties
sections.summary: The passage states support for the Bill and commends harsher penalties for altering vehicles and reckless driving, raising maximum fines from $5,000 to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my comments, Mdm Speaker, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I commend the harsher penalties for altering vehicles and reckless driving, raising the maximum fines from $5,000 to $10,000 in both cases.

sections.label: Penalty for obstructing driverless vehicles
sections.summary: The passage says the inclusion is timely for driverless vehicle innovation but notes the $5,000 maximum penalty for obstructing trials equals that for reckless driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, this inclusion is timely and necessary for Singapore to remain at the forefront of innovation for driverless vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I would like to raise the point that the maximum penalty of $5,000 for first-time offenders who obstruct driverless vehicles during trials is the same as the current penalty for first-time offenders of reckless driving.

sections.label: Regular taxi numbers 2016
sections.summary: LTA statistics in 2016 showed around 27,000 regular taxis on Singapore roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2016, LTA's statistics showed that around 27,000 regular taxis plied our roads.

sections.label: Bill requires Grab Uber registration
sections.summary: The Bill requires Grab and Uber drivers to register with LTA, complete a vocational licensing course, and undergo background screening and medical checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The changes presented by this Bill are a good start by requiring Grab and Uber drivers to register with LTA, complete a vocational licensing course and undergo background screening and medical checks.

sections.label: AV insurance bottleneck
sections.summary: Industry experts said lack of insurance is a key bottleneck for AV commercialisation, and a UK company launched the world's first self-driving car insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, industry experts whom I spoke to indicated that the lack of insurance is emerging as a key bottleneck for the full and widespread commercialisation of AVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In June last year, a UK company launched the world's first insurance for self-driving cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To accelerate the adoption of AVs in Singapore, I hope that MOT and MOF can quickly bring on board our insurance companies, even within the confines of the regulatory sandbox.

sections.label: US self-driving job estimates
sections.summary: Early US estimates show self-driving vehicles could cost the US between four to five million jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Early estimates in the US show that self-driving vehicles could cost the US between four to five million jobs.

sections.label: AV trial insurance amendments
sections.summary: The Bill mandates AV trial operators purchase liability insurance or place a deposit with LTA, and asks about penalties and liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the proposed amendments in the Bill mandates that the company or individual who wishes to carry out AV trials purchases liability insurance or places a corresponding deposit amount with LTA during the trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with us the penalties that would be imposed on those who fail to buy the appropriate insurance or place the stipulated deposit with LTA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Who would be liable should an AV hit a pedestrian or another vehicle?

sections.label: Real-time trial data transmission
sections.summary: The passage asks whether LTA would consider mandating real-time transmission of trial data to its Intelligent Transport System Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would LTA consider mandating that these trial data be transmitted real-time to LTA's Intelligent Transport System Centre?
